newsitem.title: USA: Migration from California slowing - SF Fed letter.
newsitem.headline: Migration from California slowing - SF Fed letter.

text.p: A strengthening of California labor markets in 1995 and early 1996 helped stem migration out of the state, said economists in the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco's Economic Letter.

A peak of 425,000 persons left California from July 1993 to July 1994 for better job opportunities outside the state, but economists Stuart Gabriel and Joe Mattey wrote that the tide appears to have turned, in the issue dated December 27.

A decline in California unemployment in 1995 and 1996 and recent Internal Revenue Service and California State Department of Motor Vehicles data suggest migration slowed to 250,000 persons by the end of this period, they wrote.
